Definition: literally, to load up (on the back of man or beast), i.e. to start early in the morning
BiblicalUsage: Shakam is to load up and start early, to rise before the day has begun. Abraham rose up early in the morning to take Isaac to the mountain, and the men of God through the ages rose early to their work. But the word belongs most of all to God Himself, who sent His messengers rising up betimes because He had compassion on His people, and who spoke rising up early while His people would not hear.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe God rising early to speak is the clearest picture of His patience in the whole Bible. He does not wait for us to come to Him, He comes to us at dawn, and that is why I rise early to listen.
